Questions

Why only two ingredients?
Founder Sidney Frank and cellar master François Thibault built Grey Goose around the idea that a vodka's quality comes entirely from its wheat and water — so the recipe deliberately excludes any additives, flavourings, or sugar.
Why is the water sourced from the Cognac region?
The same limestone geology that naturally filters water for cognac production filters Grey Goose's water at Gensac, contributing to its smooth, mineral character.
How should I serve it?
Best chilled, neat or on the rocks to let the texture come through, or as the base for a classic Martini, Cosmopolitan, or Vodka Tonic. Add mixers to the same order and we'll bring them together.

Questions

Why is it called Impérial?
Jean-Rémy Moët was a friend of Napoleon Bonaparte, who visited the cellars in Épernay. The cuvée created in 1869 was named Impérial in tribute to the Emperor, and the name has stayed ever since.
How do I pronounce Moët?
"Mo-wett" — the T is pronounced. The family name is Dutch in origin, so it does not follow the usual French rule of silencing the final consonant.
How much do I save on the case of six?

How long can I keep it?
Impérial is released ready to drink and is at its best within about three years. Store bottles lying down somewhere cool and dark, away from light and vibration.
